description: We are a passionate, multidisciplinary team interested in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Space Exploration, and innovative technologies. Our skills include Python programming, data analysis, problem-solving, AI model development, research, and creative thinking. We aim to combine technology, teamwork, and innovation to develop impactful, data-driven solutions to real-world challenges through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
LUNA NAV AI  is an intelligent lunar mission-planning platform designed to help mission teams evaluate landing sites and explore safer mission scenarios near the Moon's South Pole.

Choosing a lunar landing site involves more than finding flat terrain. Mission planners must also consider sunlight availability, Earth communication visibility, surface hazards, and operational constraints.

Our solution integrates NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation data with NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris information to analyze terrain, illumination, and communication conditions.

A multi-agent workflow evaluates candidate landing locations, applies mission-specific constraints, compares alternatives, and provides explainable recommendations. The platform also features interactive 3D lunar exploration, terrain-aware rover route planning, and simulated battery, communication, and operational-risk scenarios.

Unlike a simple lunar map, LUNA NAV AI connects scientific datasets with mission planning and transparent decision-making.

Our goal is to help researchers, students, and future exploration teams understand lunar mission trade-offs before launch. The project is a research prototype, not a flight-certified landing system.
details:
The Problem

The Moon's South Pole presents major challenges for exploration. A landing area may have favorable terrain but limited sunlight or communication availability. Evaluating these factors separately can overlook important mission trade-offs.

Our Solution

LUNA NAV AI combines NASA-derived lunar terrain, Sun/Earth geometry, route planning, optimization, and interactive visualization within one mission-planning platform.

Users can select a mission type, define operating constraints, and explore candidate lunar landing sites. The platform evaluates each location and presents recommendations alongside the reasoning and data-status information supporting them.

How It Works

1. Terrain Analysis

Processes NASA LOLA digital elevation data to estimate surface elevation, slope, and terrain suitability and identify candidate landing sites.

2. Illumination and Communication Analysis

Uses terrain geometry and NASA/JPL Horizons information to estimate solar illumination and direct Earth visibility during the selected mission window.

3. Surface Navigation

Applies A* pathfinding to generate terrain-aware rover routes, comparing alternative strategies such as shortest distance and gentler slopes.

4. Mission Orchestration and Optimization

Coordinates the analysis through a LangGraph-based workflow. Mission constraints are evaluated, unsuitable candidates are filtered, and feasible options are compared using optimization and scoring methods.

5. Interactive Mission Commander

Provides a browser-based mission dashboard featuring a 3D lunar explorer, mission configuration, analysis results, a surface-walk experience, and clearly labeled safety and operational simulations.

Technologies Used

  • Python for scientific computation and backend services
  • JavaScript, HTML, and WebGL for interactive visualization
  • LangGraph for multi-agent workflow orchestration
  • SciPy and optimization techniques for candidate evaluation
  • A* algorithm for rover route planning
  • NASA LRO/LOLA terrain datasets
  • NASA/JPL Horizons for astronomical geometry

What Makes LUNA NAV AI Different?

Our platform brings multiple mission-planning considerations into one explainable workflow rather than presenting isolated measurements.

It also distinguishes verified, unverified, and simulated information, helping users understand the limitations of individual outputs.

Intended Impact

LUNA NAV AI aims to make lunar mission-planning concepts more accessible, support early-stage scientific exploration, and demonstrate how NASA open data can contribute to transparent, evidence-based decision-making.

Limitations

The current system is a research prototype. Terrain resolution is approximately 240 meters per pixel in the primary dataset, limiting the detection of small hazards. Rover performance and safety scenarios use configurable assumptions. Recommendations are planning estimates and must not be interpreted as certified safe landing decisions.
